requirements.title: An access-spec requires a module specification-part
requirements.definition: An access-spec can occur only in a module specification-part. The actual syntactic context matters: a module's type definitions can contain their eligible component/binding access-specs, while a contained procedure or a submodule is not thereby the module specification-part. Separate rules govern the PRIVATE forms that are not access-spec and the permitted host access to ancestor-private entities.

requirements.title: Declaration access-specs have specific identifier subjects
requirements.definition: An access-spec in a type declaration applies to every entity name declared by that statement. In a derived-type-stmt it sets the derived type name's accessibility. In an enumeration-type-stmt it sets the enumeration type name's accessibility and the default for its enumerators. These are declarative interpretations of distinct subjects, not a propagation of type-name accessibility to every component, binding or implementation name.

requirements.title: Unspecified identifier accessibility follows its qualified default
requirements.source: 8.5.2 p3 and p4 first sentence, physical PDF120, printed106, lines11-14
requirements.definition: An identifier in the module setting whose accessibility is not explicit takes its default. The ordinary module default is PUBLIC unless changed by the relevant PRIVATE statement. The8.6.1 cross-reference is essential: a no-list statement sets the default for locally declared identifiers and applicable imports, while access statements naming used modules can determine import-specific defaults. Explicit identifier access, local declaration and the complete set of import origins retain their separate conditions.

requirements.title: Use association requires PUBLIC in the exporting module
requirements.source: 8.5.2 p4 final sentence, physical PDF120, printed106, lines15-16
requirements.definition: An identifier can be accessed from a module by use association only if it is PUBLIC in that module. This is necessary, not sufficient to bypass the USE statement's other entity, ONLY, renaming or generic restrictions. Private module identifiers may still have legitimate host/descendant, argument-associated, public-alias/binding or separate global access paths; the rule is not an undefined-value trap or a prohibition of every way to reach an entity.
